recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you factor the denominator and which factor pairs with the sine.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Factor x² − 1
steps.margin_note: First mark. x² − 1 = (x − 1)(x + 1). The (x − 1) is the factor that matches the angle inside the sine; the (x + 1) is an ordinary factor that is simply substituted at the end.
lines: At x = 1, sin(x − 1) = sin 0 = 0 and x² − 1 = 0, so the form is 0/0.

recall.must_convey: That x² − 1 is factored as (x − 1)(x + 1) so that (x − 1) pairs with sin(x − 1).
accept: factor x squared minus one as x minus one into x plus one
pair x minus one with the sine and keep x plus one separate
split it into sin x minus one over x minus one times one over x plus one
x square minus one ni x minus one into x plus one ga factor cheyyali
use the difference of squares on the denominator
heard_as: x minus one into x plus one

steps.why: The standard limit needs the same expression inside the sine and underneath it. Factoring is what produces an (x − 1) underneath to pair with the (x − 1) inside the sine.
common_mistakes: Cancelling sin(x − 1) against (x − 1) as though the sine were a multiplier.
steps.memory_tip: Whatever sits inside the sine must appear as a factor underneath. Here that is x − 1, so factor the denominator to produce it.

steps.label: Apply lim sin θ / θ = 1
steps.margin_note: Second mark. As x → 1 the angle x − 1 → 0, so the first bracket tends to 1; the second bracket is continuous at x = 1 and is substituted.
lines: As x → 1, the angle (x − 1) → 0, so lim(x → 1) sin(x − 1)/(x − 1) = 1.
The factor 1/(x + 1) is defined at x = 1, so substitute x = 1: 1/(1 + 1) = 1/2.

recall.must_convey: That sin(x − 1)/(x − 1) → 1 and 1/(x + 1) → 1/2, so the answer is 1/2.
accept: the sine part is one and one over x plus one is one half
the answer is one by two
sin x minus one over x minus one tends to one
substituting x equals one in x plus one gives two

steps.why: The two factors are handled by different rules: one by the standard limit, one by substitution, because only the first is indeterminate. The value checks numerically: at x = 1.00001 the expression is 0.4999975.
common_mistakes: Substituting x = 1 into x + 1 and writing 1 instead of 2.
steps.memory_tip: The answer is always 1 divided by the leftover factor at the point. Here the leftover is x + 1 = 2, so the answer is 1/2.

insider_note: The angle is (x − 1), so the denominator must be factorised to produce a matching (x − 1). The leftover 1/(x + 1) is then just substituted.
